Chicago Athletic Association

A private athletic club for more than a century, restored as a hotel, with Millennium Park out the windows.

Since 1893

The building

  1. Built in 1893 for the private Chicago Athletic Association.
  2. Designed by Henry Ives Cobb, with a facade by Louis Christian Mullgardt.
  3. Venetian Gothic, after the Doge’s Palace in Venice.
  4. It opened amid the 1893 World’s Columbian Exposition.
  5. A men-only club until 1972.
  6. The club closed in 2007.
  7. Restored and reopened as a hotel: architecture by Hartshorne Plunkard Architecture, interiors by Roman & Williams.
  8. Patterned brick, carved limestone, arched windows, custom stained glass, ornate plaster, and mosaic and marble floors.
  9. Views over Millennium Park and Lake Michigan.
  10. A contributing building in the Historic Michigan Boulevard District.

The spaces

Every room on these pages is one the venue offers for weddings.

which room hosts the ceremony, the cocktail hour, and the reception is not confirmed.

These are the venue’s own figures for each room; Sara and Tyler have not confirmed them yet.

  • White City Ballroom

    Floor-to-ceiling windows, vintage stained glass, an original Carrara marble floor, three 19th-century fireplaces, and 167 restored illuminated ceiling embellishments.

    Ceremony 220 · Dinner 220 · Reception 300

  • Madison Ballroom

    Original walnut parquet, historic crystal chandeliers, millwork, stained glass, and city views.

    Ceremony 220 · Dinner 120 · Reception 250

  • Stagg Court

    The club’s original basketball court and gymnasium: original flooring, hoops, and an elevated running track.

    Ceremony 300 · Dinner 250 · Reception 350

  • The Tank

    The club’s former swimming pool: original pool tile and marble pillars.

    Ceremony 175 · Dinner 130 · Reception 225
